Round 1 review of spec pose-review-ledger-is-read-once-per-operation (an engine performance change with amendment D14 of ADR governance-reads-use-bounded-operation-scoped-views; the maintainer asked for a per-operation memo after the first closeout call's profile).

What to judge: `pose-mcp/internal/pose/review_ledger_memo.go` adds `memoizedLedgerRead`, a per-key memo kept in `governanceReadViewOperation.ledgerMemo` (a sync.Map) for the life of the operation. Without an operation it computes every time. It wraps four readers: `ReadReviewRuns` now keeps the unfiltered parsed and checked runs per root (`readAllReviewRuns`, the former body) and filters by bundle on each request; `ReadReviewAttestations` keeps the whole result per (root, bundle filter) because the filter changes which losses are recorded (`readReviewAttestations`, the former body); `reviewRunTranscriptIntact` keeps the check outcome per (root, transcript path, expected digest) (`checkReviewRunTranscript`); `readReviewBundleHeader` keeps each bundle's header observation per (dir, name) (`observeReviewBundleHeader`). Callers receive copies of the top-level slices and of the loss pointer. The basis is that within one operation the read view returns the same bytes for the same read (files are cached in `v.files`; metadata in `v.observed`), so a value derived only from those reads is the same on every request; the first computation reads through the view, so the closure and final audit still cover every input. Judge: whether any of the four values depends on something other than the view's reads of that operation (for example the read budget `readBudget` of `readAllReviewRuns`, a `Now()` call, the producer, a store field other than Root, a Files without an operation, or reads routed to another root); whether a transcript check through `files.Open` is cached by the view or could see different bytes later in the same operation; whether the shallow copies are enough for every caller (grep found no caller mutating nested fields); whether errors are kept correctly; whether concurrent misses are safe. Measured on harne8 (clean clone at cc7780b1, pose-dist at 7e46b1e), one `closeout-check spec:harne8-abm-governed-execution`: before, 197 s wall and 130 s CPU, pose-dist's ledger read 280 times and 29,680 transcript checks; after, 136 s and 53 s CPU, 3 run reads and 212 checks. The remaining wall time is Git (`git log -1 -- <path>`, 1,116 calls, 81 s); a commit-graph with changed-path Bloom filters takes the first call to 59 s, recorded as follow-up F1, and keeping pure Git reads across operations as F2.

Building: this review runs under a read-only sandbox, so nothing can be built or written, not even a TMPDIR; do not try, and do not stop the review over it. The pipeline built the engine of the sealed commit and installed it as `pose` on PATH (`~/.local/bin/pose`); use that binary for read-only commands. It also ran `pose artifact-check --strict` and `pose surface-check --strict` against the sealed commit; their outputs are `/var/tmp/closeout/ac-rl.out` and `/var/tmp/closeout/sc-rl.out`. Dispose those tools from that evidence and from the code when a rerun fails for environment reasons. The package tests (`go test ./internal/pose ./internal/cli ./internal/mcpserver ./internal/scaffold`) passed on the sealed code; judge the tests by reading them.

Do NOT run `pose assess`, `pose state`, `pose index` or anything else that writes under `.pose/`; dispose assess-* tools from the sealed evidence and the code. Leave the worktree as you found it. Dispose the `validate` tools from the sealed evidence: the pipeline ran `pose validate --strict` on a clean clone of the sealed commit with a GitHub token (`.pose/results/delivery-validation.json`); a rerun in your sandbox fails for environment reasons and is not evidence about the code. A finding object accepts exactly `id`, `severity`, `disposition`, `file`, `line`, `summary`, and for an accepted follow-up `action`, `owner`, `review_by`; put any rationale inside `summary`. A new finding's id carries no round prefix (F1, F2, ...; the spec's own follow-ups are also F1 and F2, so number review findings from F3). This is round 1: `prior_findings` is empty. Sweep the whole surface and report every finding in one pass, classified blocker vs follow-up.
